conviction_note: Most of what this H1 print could add is already public: the listed subsidiaries reported in the last week (Tsuruha strong on 10-07; USMH, Ministop and Fuji weak with guidance cuts on 10-08 and 10-09; AEON FS operating profit -11%), and the Kumamoto disaster has been known since 07-30. Those offset each other, so the findings sum to 0.0. The scaled number is p_up 52 x abs 4.5 = +0.18, a slight lean because the bad news is public and the stock has already fallen 13% in 20 sessions and about 49% from January. AEON's own H1 reactions are large (2024 H1 -8.7%, 2025 H1 +9.4%), so abs_move stays near the proxy even though the sign is close to a coin flip.
bar: Full-year operating profit: company plan JPY340.0bn (unchanged at Q1, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260710/140120260707589187.pdf), IFIS consensus JPY327.5bn per a search snippet of https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=8267 (not confirmed in the document; the page fetched by curl did not render the consensus figure cleanly). There is no H1 company guide and no sourced H1 consensus. My H1 operating-profit estimate is ~JPY145bn, against ~JPY143bn if the street runs at last year's H1 progress rate (43.7% of 327.5). That bar is unsourced and derived, so every finding is capped small.
positioning_check: JPX short register 2026-09-29: no disclosed position at or above 0.5% (short_ratio 0.0, change 0.0; https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). Margin ratio 7.42 (scraped): crowded leveraged retail long, typical of a 株主優待 name. No option skew exists. run_up_20d -13.19%, run_up_5d -2.04%; priced_lean +0.22. With no short fuel and a crowded margin long, a squeeze is not available, but a visible miss would still meet sellers.

findings.finding: Tsuruha HD, AEON's consolidated health and wellness core and its biggest profit-growth driver, reported H1 operating profit of JPY54.8bn (+92.6%) and ordinary profit of JPY54.85bn on 10-07. That is 55.9% of its JPY98.1bn full-year plan against 45.7% at the same point last year, with Q2 ordinary profit +93%. So about a third of AEON's H1 operating profit came in ahead of its own pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: AEON's H1 operating-profit surprise has driven both of the last two H1 prints: 2024-10-09 (OP JPY98.6bn against a JPY115.3bn expectation) gave -8.66%, and 2025-10-14 gave +9.40% (Yahoo daily closes). AEON did not rise on Tsuruha's own release: 10-08 closed -1.3% on 15.2m shares, though that day also carried the weak food-retail subsidiaries.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Tsuruha number is public. What it adds at AEON level is the H1 consolidated print and the H&W segment margin net of PPA amortisation, which nobody can see until AEON reports. If the market had paid for it, AEON would have risen on 10-07/10-08. Instead it fell 1.3% and stayed at its low.
findings.independence: Kabutan's summary of the same release (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=3391&b=k202610070005) is the same document. A different source pointing the same way: AEON's own monthly shows Health & Wellness same-store sales 103.4/105.1/104.8/99.0/101.8 for March to July (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260910/140120260910534294.pdf).

findings.finding: AEON's food-retail and finance subsidiaries reported weak H1 numbers in the week before the print. USMH turned its full-year net forecast from +JPY0.15bn to -JPY8.0bn, with Q2 operating margin at -0.9% against -0.2%. Ministop moved to a full-year ordinary loss with an impairment. Fuji's H1 ordinary profit fell 53%. AEON Financial Service's H1 operating profit fell 11% to JPY25.2bn. This confirms the Q1 picture of GMS and supermarkets as the drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q1 (2026-07-10), GMS and SM segments were reported at an operating loss while consolidated OP hit a record, and the stock moved +1.92% close to next close. The stock has looked through this segment drag at least once.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: all four are public subsidiary releases from 10-08/09. The remaining question is whether AEON trims its JPY340bn operating plan, which it has not done at an H1 print in any of the last three years (kabuyoho revision history). If the market had not priced the drag, AEON would not be sitting at its low with -13% over 20 days.
findings.independence: Separate documents for each subsidiary: Ministop https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=9946&b=k202610080025; Fuji https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=8278&b=k202610080006; AEON FS https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20261009/140120261008548186.pdf. They are different companies but read as one theme, so they are filed as one finding.

findings.finding: The 2026 Kumamoto earthquake (07-28) destroyed AEON Mall Kumamoto in an explosion (7 dead) and closed AEON Mall Uki and 12 AEON Kyushu stores. AEON Kyushu alone booked a JPY1.745bn disaster loss in Q2, with more to come in Q3. AEON has offered all Kumamoto tenants contract termination. The consolidated extraordinary loss and any net-profit forecast cut land with this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior AEON extraordinary-loss print in the baseline. The stock fell from 1439.5 (07-29) to 1364 (07-31), about -5%, on the disaster news itself.
findings.why_not_priced: The event is known; the amount is not. AEON's 07-30 notice said the impact was under review and that it would disclose if material (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260730503374.pdf). No AEON-level 特別損失 notice appeared before the print on kabutan or TDnet. This sits below operating income on a name that trades on OP, and the outside estimate is ~JPY5bn for demolition and cleanup (gendai), small against a JPY73bn net plan. So it is sized at a fraction. A large loss, or a net-plan cut, could still meet margin longs, which is why the range is skewed negative. A modest number would read as the bad news being out.
findings.independence: Kumanichi 2026-09-11 on tenant contract terminations (https://kumanichi.com/articles/2035059); gendai 2026-08-01 cost estimate (https://gendai.media/articles/-/169757); AEON's August monthly lists the suspended stores (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260910/140120260910534294.pdf).

outside_window.finding: AEON Kyushu said the remaining earthquake costs will be booked as disaster losses from Q3 onward, and the accident investigation committee (formed 08-20) has not reported. Further Kumamoto losses and liability resolve after this window.

Returns: interim 7.50 yen already set, no buyback signal. New-year guide: not applicable (H1). baseline_tension: Run-up -13% over 20 sessions and a crowded margin long. The negatives I found (food-retail subsidiaries, Kumamoto) are public and agree with the drawdown, so they are mostly priced. The strongest positive the release could carry is a held JPY340bn plan (likely, given AEON's H1 habit) with H1 OP ahead of last year's progress on Tsuruha. I looked for a buyback or a 優待 change and found none, so the findings net to zero and only a slight lean survives.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the food-retail/AEON FS finding moved from -0.5 to -0.3, because the subsidiary releases are public.
Rule 1: the Kumamoto finding moved from -0.4 to -0.3. The event is public; only the loss amount, which the release adds, keeps it non-zero.
Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): wrote the strongest positive into baseline_tension and confirmed I searched for buybacks and 優待 changes. p_up stays at 52 because I had already looked.
